title: Redwood cost econ discovery with Cerulean Capital
summary: Discovery focused on Redwood unit economics and what levers Cerulean can use to hit a $10k/mo pilot budget. AE + SE explained per-token pricing, batching, KV prefix caching, and tradeoffs between Hosted and Dedicated/private deployments. Customer asked about latency targets, SOC2/KMS, and scheduling a benchmark pilot.
next_steps: Maya to send modeled pricing sheet for 100M tokens/month by 2026-03-06
Evan to share recommended batching/cache configuration and pilot runbook by 2026-03-09
Cerulean to confirm pilot dataset and SLA targets by 2026-03-08
Schedule 60m technical deep dive / benchmark week-of 2026-03-16
action_items: Maya: send pricing scenarios (hosted vs dedicated) - due 2026-03-06
Evan: share batching / KV cache config + sample perf numbers - due 2026-03-09
Jamie: provide sample prompt set and expected QPS for pilot - due 2026-03-08
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Evan Blake (Redwood SE), Jamie Ortiz (Head of ML, Cerulean), Priya Shah (CTO, Cerulean), Liam Cook (Infra)

[00:00] Maya:hey everybody thanks for joining, um we're excited to dig into cost and economics today.. Evan and I will run through the levers and then we can jump into your workloads and budgets
[00:18] Jamie:great thanks Maya, hi Evan, quick note — we're trying to keep this tight, main goal is figure out if Redwood Hosted can keep us inside a $10k per month pilot budget for prototyping with 20k queries/day at ~150 tokens per response
[00:33] Evan:okay cool that's helpful; quick clarifying q, is that 20k qps or 20k queries per day?
[00:40] Jamie:per day, sorry about that
[00:44] Evan:got it. so we looked at a few things: per-token list pricing, batching, and prefix/KV caching. for Hosted we bill per output token plus an input token component, and there are predictable tiers, but the big savings often come from batching and cache hits
[01:05] Priya:how big are the savings from batching? like ballpark
[01:10] Evan:very ballpark — depends on model and sequence length. with a 150 token average and small prompt sizes, you could see 1.5x to 3x cost improvement from sensible batching across similar requests. so effectively your per-token compute cost goes down because we amortize overhead across requests. but important caveat: batching adds latency; for low-latency interactive features it's tuned tightly, for async workloads you can batch more aggressively
[01:35] Liam:we're really sensitive to tail latency, sub-200ms ideally for quick chat; does batching break that?
[01:41] Evan:if you need sub-200ms tail for single-turn chat, batching isn't your main lever — you lean on dedicated capacity and smaller model variants. caching is better: prefix/KV caching can return tokens for repeated prompts instantly or reduce compute by reusing KV cache for long contexts. caching effectiveness depends on how repetitive your prompts are
[02:05] Maya:and on Hosted we offer both cost-tiered models and routing policies; if you expect predictable throughput and strict latency, Dedicated with reserved GPU pools is often the right fit, we can price that with monthly commits
[02:20] Jamie:we were hoping to avoid Dedicated for the pilot to keep friction low — is there a clear threshold where Dedicated becomes cheaper?
[02:27] Evan:yes, typically when sustained request volume pushes GPU utilization high — for text generation heavy workloads the break-even often appears around tens of millions of tokens per month depending on chosen model and quantization. Also if you want VPC/on-prem for data controls, Private changes the cost profile because of infra ops and license components
[02:50] Priya:could you unpack token math for us? we have some internal models but want to align on assumptions
[02:56] Maya:sure — basics: cost = (input_tokens + output_tokens) * per_token_rate + network/overhead in some cases. Redwood also has per-request overhead baked into throughput-backed pricing for very low-latency tiers. we'll send a pricing sheet with scenarios.
[03:18] [03:18] Speaker 2:Evan:for example, say your prompt is 50 tokens and generation is 150 tokens -> 200 tokens total. at $0.0008 per token that'd be $0.16 per request; at 20k/day that's ~ $960/day -> that's too high, so typical work is: reduce output tokens, use sampling strategies, caching for repeated prompts, and batching for throughput runs
[03:45] Jamie:that per-token number seems high compared to our expectations; what ranges do you support?
[03:50] Evan:apologies the example used a hypothetical; our public hosted rates vary by model family — e.g. smaller open models are lower cost per token but may require more latency; larger LLMs higher cost. also Redwood Optimize suggests quantization + model recommendations by workload. we'll tailor the numbers in the sheet
[04:10] Priya:we care about predictability — can we cap spend or set alerts?
[04:14] Maya:yes absolutely, Console gives token-level budgets, per-route budgets, and we can enforce hard quota. for pilots we often recommend a capped Hosted sandbox with alerts and a small Dedicated window if you need guaranteed latency
[04:30] Liam:how does KV cache hit rate look in practice? our prompts have a lot of template overlap
[04:35] Evan:if you have high template reuse you'll get 40-70% effective token savings for parts of conversations — depends on how much of the response is repeated. prefix caching is really strong for templated completions and reranking where few tokens differ
[04:52] Jamie:so practical example — 20k/day * 150 output tokens -> 3M output tokens per day? wait math, that seems off
[05:00] Evan:let's calc — 20k requests/day * 150 output tokens = 3,000,000 tokens/day -> times 30 = 90M tokens/month. right, so earlier you said 100M token pilot is a good way to model. that magnitude is where Dedicated starts to look interesting
[05:20] Priya:ok that helps. our original $10k/month target assumed 10M tokens/month, i think we misestimated the outputs
[05:27] Jamie:yeah we were optimistic — we need to refine the sample set. Jamie:action on our side — we'll provide sample prompt/response distribution
[05:35] Maya:perfect that'll let us run a more realistic cost model.
[05:40] [05:40] Speaker 3:Priya:on security we're SOC2 compliant internally, but we need to see Redwood's attestation and KMS options; can you support customer-managed keys for Private?
[05:50] Evan:yes for Private we support customer KMS/HSM and for Hosted we offer bring-your-own-key via integrated KMS — table-level audit logs and exportable traces. we can share our security pack; Maya will attach the compliance doc
[06:08] Liam:what about data residency? some of our data must stay in eu-west region
[06:12] Maya:we have hosted regions in eu-west and also private deployments. for pilot, we can provision regionally isolated hosted endpoints.
[06:22] Jamie:what about model fallbacks? if the preferred model is unavailable can requests route to a cheaper variant?
[06:27] Evan:yes routing policies can route by latency/cost/region. we also do automatic compatible-variant fallback which keeps requests alive albeit with different perf/cost profiles
[06:40] Priya:training-like costs for fine-tuning — out of scope for this pilot, right?
[06:44] Maya:correct, pilot focuses on inference economics; we can discuss fine-tune lifecycle later — but cost model is different (training vs inference)
[06:52] [07:00] Evan:lets walk through a sample model of cost per 100M tokens: scenario A hosted with moderate batching and 30% cache hit — scenario B Dedicated with monthly commit and optimized batching. the sheet will show per-token effective costs and break-even months
[07:18] Jamie:can you briefly explain what dedicated commit pricing looks like? upfront vs overage?
[07:22] Maya:sure — Dedicated is a monthly reserved capacity cost (commit) plus a lower marginal per-token compute for extra headroom; you can choose a flat monthly fee that includes a set throughput. overages are billed at a discounted rate relative to Hosted list
[07:40] Liam:if we do Dedicated how long is the min term?
[07:44] Maya:we do month-to-month for pilot-focused dedicated pools, but enterprise contracts go annual. we can do a 3-month pilot commit as well depending on need
[07:54] Jamie:pricing sensitivity — our CFO will want an ROI slide. can you help build a model comparing ours to OpenAI and Anthropic?
[08:03] Evan:we can produce a competitive cost-comparison; note the apples-to-apples problem — models differ in output token length, latency, and quality. we'll include quantization and batching assumptions so it's transparent
[08:20] Priya:there's also inference hardware choices — are you sourcing A100s, H100s, or cheaper T4-like instances behind the scenes?
[08:28] Evan:for Hosted we mix depending on model family; high-performance low-latency models run on H100-like instances, while cost-optimized pipelines may use 4-bit quantized runtimes on more efficient hardware. Dedicated gives you more control over instance class as part of the commit
[08:46] Jamie:we'd like a pilot that demonstrates both cost and latency targets — can Redwood run a week-long benchmark with our prompt set?
[08:53] Maya:yes we do that often; typical pilot is 1 week of run traces + 1 week of load testing, we collect tokens, latencies, and cost breakdown, and provide a runbook and expected config. Evan will own the technical run
[09:07] Evan:for the benchmark we'll need a representative prompt set, expected QPS, and desired SLOs. we'll instrument with traces and give per-route token maps so you can see hot prompts that would benefit from caching
[09:20] Jamie:ok we'll pull that together. question — in Dedicated is price per token fixed? or do you still have model-based token multipliers?
[09:27] Maya:Dedicated reduces marginal compute, but model choice still influences effective cost because different models produce different token counts and runtime characteristics; the commit buys you GPU time and lower per-token processing overhead
[09:41] Priya:what about function calling and tool integrations, does that affect billing?
[09:46] Evan:function calls still consume tokens for prompts and responses, but we also show them separately in Console so you can see usage by route. there isn't a separate line item for 'tool calls' aside from tokens and request overhead
[09:59] Liam:we have a lot of reranking tasks that use embeddings; can embeddings be cheaper?
[10:04] Evan:we price embeddings per 1K vectors; embeddings are typically much cheaper per unit and Redwood Optimize can recommend when to precompute and cache embeddings to avoid repeated costs
[10:15] Jamie:let's talk about implementation complexity — if we start Hosted with a budget cap and later move to Dedicated, how disruptive is the switch?
[10:23] Maya:we design the APIs and model pins so switching is straightforward at the routing layer — you'd retarget routes to dedicated endpoints and update rollout policies. some infra work for VPC / network will be needed for Private but it's not a full rewrite
[10:38] Priya:do you do autoscaling on Dedicated? what about burst capacity?
[10:42] Evan:Dedicated supports configurable autoscaling policies and an option for burst capacity into shared pools; the burst is throttled and billed differently but it's useful for traffic spikes
[10:52] Jamie:ok this is all super helpful. can we get a sample pricing scenario right now rough on the call?
[10:57] Maya:sure, quick simple estimate: if we assume 90M tokens/month (from the earlier calc) and Hosted effective rate of $0.00006 per token after batching/caching and smaller models, that's ~$5,400/month. Dedicated with a modest commit might be $4k/month plus lower marginals — but exact numbers depend on model and cache hits. this is high-level
[11:22] Jamie:that puts us in range but depends a ton on cache hit rates and model choice. we'll return with sample prompts
[11:28] Evan:also consider prompt engineering to reduce output lengths or split logic to smaller completions — that can move the needle faster than switching infra sometimes
[11:38] Priya:we'll share an initial sample set by Monday, want to confirm who to send it to?
[11:42] Maya:send to maya@redwood.com and cc evan@redwood.com, and we'll ingest and run a cost projection
[11:48] Liam:question on logs — we need audit logs for every token request for compliance, is that available
[11:54] Evan:yes, Console includes request-level traces and audit logs; for Private you get a full control plane and raw access to logs, Hosted has exportable logs and configurable retention
[12:07] [12:07] Speaker 2:Jamie:ok last question on quotas: can you set per-route hard limits so we don't explode spend in a misbehaving route?
[12:14] Maya:yes hard route quotas are supported and we'll help set conservative defaults for the pilot
[12:20] Priya:are there any hidden costs we should plan for? e.g., network egress or storage for cached KV?
[12:26] Evan:network egress only in cross-region scenarios; KV cache and prefix store are included in the inference pricing for Hosted within normal usage; if you go Private, storage and infra ops are accounted for in the package

[12:40] Jamie:cool. let's recap next steps
[12:44] Maya:recap — we will: 1) send pricing sheet with modeled scenarios (Maya) 2) Evan share batching/cache config + pilot runbook 3) Cerulean to share sample prompts and QPS 4) schedule technical deep dive / benchmark week-of Mar 16
[12:58] Priya:agree
[13:00] Jamie:thanks all, we'll follow up via email and attach sample datasets
[13:04] Maya:thanks everyone!

[End of transcript]
